name: Persinger lab: burst-firing through both temporal lobes (20 min)
origin: Laurentian University Behavioural Neuroscience Laboratory (Persinger, Koren, Richards)
summary: The Persinger lab's bilateral burst-firing exposure: the 230-point pattern (3-ms points, 0.69 s) with 4 s between presentations, switched round four left-right coil pairs every 0.5 s, equal on both sides, for 20 min. It is the 'both hemispheres' arm of Healey 1996 and Persinger & Healey 2002, where the lab reports no change in suggestibility but the highest presence score.
notes: Healey 1996 played 230 points of 3 ms through a helmet with four solenoids per side, the field going to each left-right pair in turn, once round every 2 s (pp.2-3 [202-203]). Persinger & Healey 2002 report the same 48 people and give 4 s between presentations (p.3 [535]): that is the pause, not the cycle (Persinger 1999 p.3 [165]). This program plays 0.69 s on and 4 s off: one left-right pair is on at a time, and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. The burst is the project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers (the lab prints the shape only as a small figure: Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). Field: the papers differ: 1 to 5 uT over an activated hemisphere, place not given (Healey 1996 p.3 [203]); 100 nT near the midpoint and 1 uT along the inside of the helmet (Persinger & Healey 2002 p.3 [535]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Support: this arm did not differ from sham on suggestibility (Healey 1996 p.4 [204]) and had the highest presence score (0.8, SD 0.6; Persinger & Healey 2002 Table 2, p.4 [536]). Richards 1993 used an earlier 1-ms form. The rise in aggression in Gillis 1993 was in the group given the pattern without pauses (p.2 [169]; persinger-gillis-1993-continuous-bilateral). One lab. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Compare blind with persinger-healey-burst-right, persinger-healey-burst-left and sham. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Blindfolded or with opaque goggles, reclining in a quiet, dark room (the lab used a grounded acoustic chamber of 2.74 x 2.54 x 1.98 m and asked people to notice whatever happens without labelling it).
schedule: One 20-min exposure; Gillis & Persinger gave three, one week apart. At most once a week.
